question.worked_solution:
Using the linearity property of double integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{1+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y}{x}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}(\frac{1}{x}+\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{R}\frac{1}{x}\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the first integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{1}{x}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(\pi -0){\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi \cdot [\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|]_{1}^{e} \\  & =\pi (\operatorname{ln}⁡e-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the second integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\text{ }\text{d}A & =(e-1){\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y \\  & =(e-1)[-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(e-1)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =2(e-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{1+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y}{x}\,\text{d}A=\pi +2(e-1)=2e+\pi -2.\end{aligned}
$$
